findings.problem: The style guide sets chapters 1-8 as dialogue-forward procedural at about 60:40 dialogue to narration. Words inside quotation marks are about 12% of this chapter (2,600 of 22,000), and the share is level across every section. Part of that is legitimate: the ward vigil and the loft fight are solitary or wordless. But the core clue-gathering of B5, the aha the plan's craft research says to slow down for, is delivered as reported speech in one 200-word paragraph (line 471). The patients who give Jaina the answer never speak in their own voices. The same happens with Tobin's well sorting (433) and the first round of new cases (251).
findings.fix: Dramatize line 471 as a short run of direct exchanges: Jaina asks, and the cooper's wife answers in her door-hinge voice ('Two a day from Ellen's mam. Five of us, and who's time to bake?'), then Elsie, then Hew Dunmore without lifting his eyes ('She eats the heel standing up. Says it's the best of it.'). Keep Jaina's questions short and in her civilian downshift register. Col's lines at 475-479 already work this way and show the model. Line 251 can give the young man his 'Tobin's an old woman' line as direct speech. Do not pad the night vigil with talk to raise the ratio; B4, B5 and B11 are where dialogue belongs.

findings.problem: The style guide sets narrative distance as 'no italicized internal monologue, no thought-tags; narration IS the character thinking'. These lines break it with 'she thought' tags or italic thoughts: 713 ('she thought, very clearly, *they should have left me...*'), 727 ('had half a heartbeat to think *good, he's frightened, he'll talk*'), 853 ('Crying again, she thought.'), 859 ('a little, she thought'), 1043 ('she thought, from a long way off, *good, that's the embers seen to,*'), 345 ('*No. No, I didn't—*'), 595 (italic). findings.fix: Render each as plain free indirect narration in roman type. 713: 'They should have left her by the water butt.' 727: 'Good, he was frightened, he'd talk—' 853: 'Crying again. She couldn't hear it. She didn't look.' (909 'Crying, she'd thought' can stay: that is a recollection, and it pays off.) 1043: 'Good. findings.passage: And the carter on the bridge had asked them, so friendly, if they'd passed a young fellow with a grain cart. ... Sylvanas had stood on that bridge. She had stood half in the doorway at the inn while the girl talked. Jaina looked at her, and Sylvanas looked back, and neither of them said it.
findings.problem: The B7 planner warning says the old carter stays unidentified and is not mentioned as a suspect, because Ch5 owns that snag on Sylvanas's side. 'So friendly' puts an edge on the carter, and the next paragraph, where both women look at each other and 'neither of them said it', makes the unspoken 'it' read as a shared suspicion of the carter rather than the resemblance between the Millhaven grain-man and this one. Jaina is the POV, and here she seems to be making the connection Ch5 is meant to make.
findings.fix: Cut 'so friendly'. Either drop the carter clause entirely and let the girl's 'Cheaper than Mister Hollis' carry the resemblance alone, or keep the carter as a neutral source ('the carter on the bridge had asked after a young fellow with a grain cart'). Make the unsaid 'it' plainly the supplier: one new man selling cheap at Millhaven and here.

findings.passage: He looked at it the way the little ones in the cathedral at Boralus used to look at the reliquary... / She looked at him for a long moment, the way she'd looked at him in the lane before noon... / the way she had let him look at his own street...
findings.problem: 'The way' is the chapter's default simile and callback frame: 53 uses in 22k words, four in twenty lines at 927-945. Several are narrator generalisations in the second person ('the way you would hold a gate shut', 'the way you lift a full bowl', 'the voice you would use to a son', 'the way you shake after a long night on deck'). These pull the camera slightly out from Jaina. Individually most are good, but together they are a tic.
findings.fix: Cut or recast about half. Keep the ones that carry Jaina's own memory (Boralus, Antonidas's letters, the nurse's cheek). Turn plain manner clauses into direct description ('She looked at him for a long moment, hands at her sides, as she had in the lane'). Anchor the second-person ones to Jaina's experience ('the way she'd shaken after a night watch on her father's deck').

findings.passage: The boy's face was wet. He'd been crying, silently, the whole time.
findings.problem: 'The whole time' is something Jaina can't know. She had her back half to him while she laid the shell and read the spill. It is a small omniscient step.
findings.fix: Make it her inference: 'The boy's face was wet. He must have been crying since the frost went over him, and she hadn't heard a sound.'

findings.passage: The whole cooper's household was down, Tobin had said, all five of them
findings.problem: The counts don't agree. On the page Tobin never says the whole cooper's household is down: at 251 he names only the boy and the mother. At 445 the house is 'down to the last child', which is ambiguous. The slate at 429, written for 'everyone in this room', lists six names, but at 855 there are 'seven wards'. The room description at 169-171 suggests more patients than six. A careful reader doing the sums alongside Jaina will trip on it, and it touches the procedural spine of B5.
findings.fix: Choose one count and make it consistent: either have Tobin say at 251 that all five of the cooper's house are down, with the others on pallets, and put them on the slate, or cut 'all five' and make 855 'six wards'. Flag it for the continuity gate as well.

checkResults.emotional-life: pass. Jaina thinks on the page in every beat, in her own idiom, and argues with herself in the way her sheet describes: question, wrong answer, 'No. Slower', a better answer (23, 279, 313, 439-449, 505-509, 999-1005). Registers include dry humour (143 the hat, 255 'sold him a bad horse', 405 'Did you just bite my bandage?', 501 'Shall we have a prize-giving?', 1131), warmth (31 Boralus herring, the knot, 1053 Elsie cool), horror (the cage), and exhaustion (the vigil). The value shifts land on concrete moments: the spear grounded, Wenna going still, the slate, 'On purpose', the frost, the foam, the cold chimney, the sacking stencil. The voices are distinct: Brask, Tobin, Cyndia, Lyriel and Sylvanas could not swap lines.
checkResults.voice-and-register: Partial. Paragraph shape is varied (mean 3.1 sentences, no runs of three or more single-sentence narration paragraphs). Dialogue tags are almost all 'said'. The narration belongs to Jaina. The issues are a low dialogue share against the procedural target, 'the way' overuse, and one stock phrase.
checkResults.limited-third: Mostly clean: Sylvanas's reasoning for the sleeve shot is withheld (739), and B6 stays on what Jaina can see through glass. The failures are thought tags and italic monologue, plus one 'the whole time'.
checkResults.dialogue-register: Clean. No institutional or clinical vocabulary. Jaina downshifts for civilians, gives Sylvanas the full reasoning in B7, and stays polite and immovable with Brask ('I'm sorry, Captain. Every house.'). There are two 'not X, Y' constructions.
checkResults.beat-fidelity: All twelve beats (B1-B11a) are dramatized, none summarized. Lyriel's switch to 'Jaina' lands in the knot lesson, with the fixed line verbatim. Jaina says only 'Ranger-General' aloud. Andorhal has an on-page source in the stencilled sacking and Brask. Brask's ledger, spelling and 'tell it right' come with no farewell blessing. Smaller problems: the carter edge at 641-643, the 'bread bin' at 325, and the patient counts.

summary: A strong draft on story and character. Every beat is dramatized, Jaina's free indirect argument with herself is the best on the series so far, and the voices are clearly separate. It fails on texture: 64.2/100, with almost no participial connective tissue, compound joins at twice the target, and em-dashes at a quarter of it. Below that sit a dialogue share far under the procedural target (the B5 interviews are reported speech), thought tags and italic monologue against the narrative-distance rule, and a carter aside in B7 that steps on Ch5's snag. The smaller items are 'not X, Y' lines, one stock 'breath' phrase, the 'the way' tic, a bread pre-signal and patient-count drift.
